answer: An agent market for garden care at dawn requires each bidder, whether forecasting rain or a zephyr, to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before its account can submit bids. The bond stays locked even if the account leaves early. Creating names is cheap, but activating 10,000 fake bidders ties up $1 million for a month. This does not prove unique identity; it makes a swarm costly in proportion to its size.
